config.title: Micro-frontend Shell

intro.title: Micro-frontend Shell
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a micro-frontend shell application using Vue. This shell acts as a main container that dynamically loads and displays separate micro-frontend applications. You will learn how to use Vue's component system and dynamic imports to manage and integrate these independent modules. The core programming concept involves modular architecture and lazy loading for efficient code splitting. Key technologies include Vue components, JavaScript modules, and the Vue Router for navigation. By the end, you'll have a functional shell that can host multiple micro-frontends, demonstrating scalable frontend development.
intro.usecase: Micro-frontend shells are commonly used in large-scale enterprise applications where different teams work on independent modules. For example, a banking dashboard might have separate micro-frontends for account balances, transaction history, and investment portfolios, all loaded into a single shell application. E-commerce platforms use this pattern to combine product listings, shopping carts, and recommendation engines from different services. This approach allows teams to deploy updates independently while maintaining a cohesive user interface.

objectives: Construct a Vue shell application to serve as the host container for micro-frontends
Configure dynamic component loading to render micro-frontends on demand
Implement a shared state management system for communication between the shell and micro-frontends
Initialize and control routing within the shell to navigate between different micro-frontends
Apply CSS isolation techniques to prevent style conflicts between the shell and micro-frontends
Integrate a build configuration that supports independent deployment of micro-frontends
Manulate lifecycle hooks to manage the loading and unloading of micro-frontends

steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from the Vue package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary functions from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing functions from a module
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and createApp functions are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported something, but make sure to import both Vue and createApp from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import Vue and createApp from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App with a template section that returns a root div element.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define a component using an object with a template property. The template should contain a single root element, typically a div.

// Import Vue and createApp here

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component defined with a template that returns a div element.
successCriteria: An App component is defined with a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your App component has a template property with a div element inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined. Check that you've created a component object with a template containing a div.

steps.title: Initialize micro-frontend routes data
steps.instruction: In your App component, create a data function that returns an array of micro-frontend route objects. Each object should have properties like 'name', 'path', and 'url'.
steps.hint: In Vue, components can have a data function that returns an object containing reactive data. For this step, return an array of objects from the data function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a data function that returns an array of route objects, setting up the foundation for micro-frontend routing.
successCriteria: The App component contains a data function that returns an array with at least one route object having properties like name, path, and url.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your data function returns an array of objects with properties like name, path, and url.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data function is missing or doesn't return the expected array of route objects. Check the syntax and structure.

steps.title: Add active micro-frontend state
steps.instruction: In the App component's data function, add a property called 'activeMicroFrontend' with an initial value of null.
steps.hint: Add 'activeMicroFrontend: null' inside the data function's return object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a reactive data property to track which micro-frontend is currently active.
successCriteria: The data function returns an object containing 'activeMicroFrontend: null'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added 'activeMicroFrontend: null' inside the data function's return object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The active micro-frontend state wasn't properly added. In Vue, reactive data properties go inside the data function's return object.

steps.title: Create navigation handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's methods object, create a method named 'setActiveMicroFrontend' that takes a route parameter and updates the activeMicroFrontend state with that route.
steps.hint: Add a methods property to your component configuration and define the function there. The function should update this.activeMicroFrontend with the provided route.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a method that can be called to change the active micro-frontend when a navigation item is clicked.
successCriteria: A methods object exists with a setActiveMicroFrontend function that updates this.activeMicroFrontend.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a methods object with a function that updates the activeMicroFrontend state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation handler isn't set up correctly. Check that you've added a methods object with a setActiveMicroFrontend function that updates the component state.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, add a main div container with a header element containing the text 'Micro-frontend Shell' and a content area div.
steps.hint: Add a template section to your component with a main container div, then add a header and content area inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a basic layout structure with a header and content area ready to hold micro-frontend content.
successCriteria: The App component has a template with a main div container containing a header element with text 'Micro-frontend Shell' and a content area div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a main div container with both a header (containing 'Micro-frontend Shell') and a content area div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing or incomplete. Add a main div container with a header and content area.

steps.title: Add header with application title
steps.instruction: Inside the template of your App component, add a header element containing an h1 with the text 'Micro-frontend Shell'.
steps.hint: Add a <header> element with an <h1> inside it. Place this at the beginning of your template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a header with a title

My Application
steps.expectedOutcome: The shell application will have a visible header with the title 'Micro-frontend Shell' displayed at the top.
successCriteria: The template contains a <header> element with an <h1> element inside it displaying the text 'Micro-frontend Shell'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some structure, but make sure you have both the <header> element and an <h1> inside it with the exact text 'Micro-frontend Shell'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header with the application title wasn't added correctly. Check that you have a <header> element containing an <h1> with the text 'Micro-frontend Shell' in your template.

steps.title: Create navigation menu
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a <nav> element with an unordered list (<ul>) that will contain navigation items for the micro-frontend routes.
steps.hint: Add the <nav> element within the main container structure, then include a <ul> inside it. You'll add list items in a later step.

steps.expectedOutcome: A navigation structure is added to the template, ready to hold navigation items for micro-frontend routes.
successCriteria: The template contains a <nav> element with a <ul> inside it, placed within the main container structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the <nav> element and the <ul> inside it within the main container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation structure isn't complete. Add a <nav> element with a <ul> inside it to create the navigation menu.

steps.title: Display micro-frontend routes in navigation
steps.instruction: Inside your component's template, add a <nav> element with an unordered list (<ul>) that uses v-for to iterate through the microFrontends array and display each route as a list item (<li>) with a button.
steps.hint: Place the <nav> element after the header. Use v-for on the <li> tag to loop through microFrontends, and add a button inside each <li> that displays the route name.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: rendering list items from an array
steps.expectedOutcome: A navigation menu appears below the header with three list items (Dashboard, Analytics, Settings), each containing a button.
successCriteria: The template contains a <nav> element with a <ul> that uses v-for to iterate through microFrontends and renders each as an <li> with a button displaying the route name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added navigation structure, but make sure you're using v-for correctly to iterate through microFrontends and display each route name in a button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation menu isn't displaying the micro-frontend routes. Check that you've added the <nav> element with <ul> and used v-for to loop through microFrontends.

steps.title: Wire navigation click events
steps.instruction: In the navigation menu, add click event handlers to each list item that call the setActiveMicroFrontend method with the corresponding micro-frontend id.
steps.hint: Use @click (or v-on:click) on the <li> elements and pass the micro-frontend id to the handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each navigation item will have a click handler that calls setActiveMicroFrontend with the correct micro-frontend id when clicked.
successCriteria: All three list items have @click (or v-on:click) handlers that call setActiveMicroFrontend with the corresponding micro-frontend id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some click handlers, but not all navigation items are wired. Make sure each <li> has an @click handler that calls setActiveMicroFrontend with the correct id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation items don't have click handlers yet. Add @click (or v-on:click) to each <li> element to call setActiveMicroFrontend with the micro-frontend id.
